planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Karasuba carries deeply lobed, maple-like leaves that emerge burgundy-red in spring and hold tinges of that color through the season, deepening again in fall, a richer coloring than the plain green species. Loose sprays of small white, star-shaped flowers rise above the foliage in early spring before the leaves fully expand. Plant in humus-rich, consistently moist, well-drained soil in partial to full shade, where it slowly spreads to form a textured groundcover. Divide congested clumps in spring or fall to control spread or propagate new plants.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun.

directions: Sakura bears clusters of soft pink, cherry-blossom-toned flowers held above large, glossy, rounded leaves that take on bronze-red tones through winter. Like other bergenia it tolerates both sun and considerable shade, making it a versatile edging or groundcover plant for the front of a mixed border. Plant in moist, well-drained soil and divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor. Its evergreen foliage provides winter structure even when not in bloom.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in consistently moist to wet soil in partial shade to full sun near a pond margin or rain garden.

directions: Bowles Golden forms an upright clump of brilliant golden-yellow, grass-like blades that light up a pond margin or damp border, holding color best with some direct sun. It tolerates standing water at the root zone as well as consistently moist garden soil, making it a reliable choice for the wet edge of a water feature. Small brown flower spikes appear in late spring but are secondary to the foliage display. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain a tidy, vigorous stand.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in average, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun.

directions: Charlotte's Web produces clusters of three-petaled purple-blue flowers over grassy, arching foliage from early summer into fall, each bloom lasting only a day but renewing in steady succession. It tolerates both partial shade and full sun, adapting its habit slightly denser in brighter light. Plant in average, well-drained soil and cut the clump back by half in midsummer if foliage becomes floppy, which encourages a fresh flush of flowers. Divide every few years in spring to keep plantings vigorous.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade.

directions: Chantilly Lace (PP30740) is a compact goat's beard selection that sends up airy, creamy-white plumes above finely cut, fern-like foliage in early summer, on a scale suited to smaller shade gardens than the larger species. It needs consistently moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade, declining quickly if allowed to dry out. The feathery flower plumes persist attractively for several weeks and can be left standing for texture after bloom fades. Divide congested clumps in spring every few years to maintain vigor.
